BIOL 101.description: Introductory survey of macromolecules, cell structure and function, genetics, and molecular biology.
BIOL 101.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101.title: Biological Principles I

BIOL 101A.description: Introductory survey of macromolecules, cell structure and function, genetics, and molecular biology. Three lecture hours per week. Restricted to students who have credit for BIOL 101L but lack the lecture.
BIOL 101A.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101A.title: Biological Principles I

BIOL 101L.description: (Recommended concurrent with BIOL 101 ). Experimental examination of basic principles of cell biology, genetics and metabolism. Three hours per week.
BIOL 101L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101L.title: Biological Principles I Laboratory

BIOL 102.description: Introductory survey of plant and animal development, physiology, ecology, and evolution.
BIOL 102.subject: BIOL
BIOL 102.title: Biological Principles II

BIOL 102A.description: Introductory survey of plant and animal development, physiology, ecology, and evolution. Three lecture hours per week. Restricted to students who have credit for BIOL 102L but lack the lecture.
BIOL 102A.subject: BIOL
BIOL 102A.title: Biological Principles II

BIOL 102L.description: Experimental examination of structure and function of plant and animal systems, biodiversity, ecology. BIOL 101 , BIOL 102 , BIOL 101L and BIOL 102L must be completed prior to enrolling in 300 -level or above Biology courses.
BIOL 102L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 102L.title: Biological Principles II Laboratory

BIOL 110.description: Basic biological concepts and issues for non-biology majors. Credit may not be given for both this course and BIOL 120 . Three lecture, two laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 110.subject: BIOL
BIOL 110.title: General Biology

BIOL 120.description: Fundamental principles of human biology. Credit may not be given for both BIOL 110 and BIOL 120. Three lecture hours per week. Not for major credit.
BIOL 120.subject: BIOL
BIOL 120.title: Human Biology

BIOL 120L.description: Exercises dealing with basic concepts of human biology. Not for major credit.
BIOL 120L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 120L.title: Laboratory in Human Biology

BIOL 200.description: An introduction to plant science for the non-major. This course does not carry major credit, and is not designed as a prerequisite for other biology courses. Plant development, physiology, genetics, evolution, and ecology will be considered. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 200.subject: BIOL
BIOL 200.title: Plant Science

BIOL 200L.description: Laboratory exercises, demonstrations, and audio-visual supplements to BIOL 200 . Not for major credit. Two hours per week.
BIOL 200L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 200L.title: Plant Science Laboratory

BIOL 202.description: An introduction to pathogens including bacteria, viruses, and protozoans. Basic elements of the immune system coupled with discussion of how pathogens cause disease. This information is placed in the context of how scientific research leads to the discovery, treatment, and prevention of the disease. The ethical implications of each pathogen and its treatment strategies are discussed.
BIOL 202.subject: BIOL
BIOL 202.title: Infectious Diseases, Human Health, and Ethics

BIOL 203.description: This class goes beyond the classroom to visit sites affected by infectious diseases, like cholera and bubonic plague, in order to put these diseases into context, gaining a deeper understanding of the implications of infectious disease on human health and ethics. This course will experience infectious diseases through the scope of art, literature, and architecture.
BIOL 203.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in BIOL 202.
BIOL 203.subject: BIOL
BIOL 203.title: Exploration of Infectious Diseases

BIOL 206.description: (Designed for non-major students.) Genetic principles, emphasizing human heredity. Relevance of recent advances in genetics. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 206.subject: BIOL
BIOL 206.title: Genetics and Society

BIOL 208.description: Scientific and social issues concerning the interrelationship of culture and agricultural biotic diversity and technology, climate change, resources management, food security, and human health.
BIOL 208.subject: BIOL
BIOL 208.title: Our Hungry World from Malthus to McDonalds

BIOL 210.description: The study of domestic dogs (Canis lupus familiaris) and their relatives. Genetics, evolution, behavior, and physiology in dogs.
BIOL 210.subject: BIOL
BIOL 210.title: The Biology of Dogs

BIOL 220.description: This course will ensure that elementary education majors will understand the fundamental concepts of Biology. Cannot be used for biology major credit.
BIOL 220.subject: BIOL
BIOL 220.title: Elementary Life Science

BIOL 232.description: Functional anatomy of the human body and its relation to disease processes. Not for biology major credit.
BIOL 232.subject: BIOL
BIOL 232.title: Anatomy

BIOL 232L.description: The principles of anatomy as demonstrated by microscopic studies and animal dissection. Three hours per week.
BIOL 232L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 232L.title: Anatomy Laboratory

BIOL 240.description: Fundamentals of functional human biology and knowledge of contemporary medical problems. Not for major credit.
BIOL 240.subject: BIOL
BIOL 240.title: Applied Human Physiology

BIOL 242.description: Functional biology of organ systems in the maintenance of the whole organism; homeostatic relationships. Not available for biology major credit. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 242.subject: BIOL
BIOL 242.title: Human Physiology

BIOL 243.description: Functional anatomy and physiology of the human body, including the integumentary, skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems. Not available for biology major credit. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 243.subject: BIOL
BIOL 243.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology I

BIOL 243L.description: The principles of anatomy and physiology as demonstrated by microscopic studies, animal dissection, and physiological experiments. One three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 243L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 243L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Laboratory

BIOL 244.description: Functional anatomy and physiology of the human body, including the cardiovascular, endocrine, excretory, reproductive, digestive, and respiratory systems. Not available for biology major credit. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 244.subject: BIOL
BIOL 244.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology II

BIOL 244L.description: A continuation of BIOL 243L . One three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 244L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 244L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Laboratory

BIOL 250.description: An introduction to bacteria and viruses, emphasizing structure, metabolism, and pathogenesis. Discussion of infectious diseases, antigen-antibody relationships, and anti-microbial agents in chemotherapy. Not available for biology major credit. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 250.subject: BIOL
BIOL 250.title: Microbiology

BIOL 250L.description: Not available for biology major credit. Three hours per week.
BIOL 250L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 250L.title: Microbiology Laboratory

BIOL 260.description: Physiology of human systems especially susceptible to disturbance: immunobiology, circulation, excretion, metabolism, endocrinology, and muscle physiology. Not for biology major credit. Intended for pharmacy students.
BIOL 260.subject: BIOL
BIOL 260.title: Physiology

BIOL 270.description: Basic ecological principles and the impacts of human population growth and technology. Not for major credit.
BIOL 270.subject: BIOL
BIOL 270.title: Introduction to Environmental Biology

BIOL 270L.description: Demonstrations, data analyses, discussions, and films relating to human ecology, resource use, and environmental impact. Not for major credit. Two hours per week.
BIOL 270L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 270L.title: Introduction to Environmental Biology Laboratory

BIOL 301.description: Concepts of evolution, populations, and population interactions; communities and ecosystems. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 301.subject: BIOL
BIOL 301.title: Ecology and Evolution

BIOL 301L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations. Three hours per week.
BIOL 301L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 301L.title: Ecology and Evolution Laboratory

BIOL 302.description: Principles of eukaryotic cell structure, molecular organization, and physiology. Genome organization and expression. Cell growth, division, and cell-cell interactions.
BIOL 302.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 101; C or better in BIOL 102 or MSCI 311; C or better in CHEM 112 or CHEM 142.
BIOL 302.subject: BIOL
BIOL 302.title: Cell and Molecular Biology

BIOL 302L.description: Experiments, exercises, and demonstrations. Three hours per week.
BIOL 302L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 302L.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Laboratory

BIOL 303.description: Basic principles of transmission and molecular genetics; quantitative inheritance; recombination; biochemical aspects of gene function and regulation; developmental genetics and population genetics. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 303.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 101 and BIOL 102 or a C or better in MSCI 311.
BIOL 303.subject: BIOL
BIOL 303.title: Fundamental Genetics

BIOL 303L.description: Observational and experimental examination of principles of genetics and inheritance.
BIOL 303L.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 101, BIOL 101L, BIOL 102, and BIOL 102L or a C or better in MSCI 311.
BIOL 303L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 303L.title: Fundamental Genetics Laboratory

BIOL 351.description: Exploration of current careers in the animal industry including a brief overview of the sciences involved in animal production such as genetics and selection, behavior, physiology, reproduction, and nutrition of cattle (beef and dairy), horses, swine, sheep, poultry, and others.
BIOL 351.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 102.
BIOL 351.subject: BIOL
BIOL 351.title: Introduction to Animal Science

BIOL 351L.description: Explorations into the use of animals in various industries in today’s society.
BIOL 351L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 351L.title: Introduction to Animal Science Laboratory

BIOL 398.description: Participation in preparation and teaching of undergraduate biological sciences laboratories.
BIOL 398.subject: BIOL
BIOL 398.title: Laboratory Teaching Experience

BIOL 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department head is required for undergraduate students.
BIOL 399.subject: BIOL
BIOL 399.title: Independent Study

BIOL 405.description: Cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying the development and functions of the nervous system, such as nervous system patterning, neuronal differentiation/migration, formation of neuronal projections, development of synapses, apoptosis, refinement of neuronal circuits, and how cells and neurons respond to signals from the environment.
BIOL 405.subject: BIOL
BIOL 405.title: Cellular and Molecular Neurobiology

BIOL 415.description: Phylogenetic and comparative aspects of anatomy, reproduction, and embryology of the vertebrates. Three lecture hours and one three-hour laboratory period per week.
BIOL 415.subject: BIOL
BIOL 415.title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy

BIOL 420.description: Phylogenetic survey of the major plant divisions; consideration of the structure and development of flowering plants.
BIOL 420.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301.
BIOL 420.subject: BIOL
BIOL 420.title: Survey of the Plant Kingdom

BIOL 420L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 420L.title: Survey of the Plant Kingdom Laboratory

BIOL 423.description: A survey of plants affecting human health and how they are used historically and in modern times, with emphasis on the biologically active constituents.
BIOL 423.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301 and BIOL 302.
BIOL 423.subject: BIOL
BIOL 423.title: Medicinal Botany

BIOL 425.description: Basic introduction to plants, including cellular biology, energetics, structure-function relationships, development, nutrition, and diversity.
BIOL 425.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302.
BIOL 425.subject: BIOL
BIOL 425.title: Plant Form and Function

BIOL 425L.description: Illustration of principles of introductory botany and plant physiology using experiments, exercises, and demonstrations. Three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 425L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 425L.title: Plant Form and Function Laboratory

BIOL 426.description: Structure and dynamics of plant populations and communities, including life histories, adaptations, and plant interactions.
BIOL 426.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 301 and BIOL 303.
BIOL 426.subject: BIOL
BIOL 426.title: Plant Ecology

BIOL 426L.description: Laboratory and field exercises in plant ecology.
BIOL 426L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 426L.title: Plant Ecology Laboratory

BIOL 450.description: Principles and methods of measuring production in the sea. Emphasis on the ocean’s role in the global carbon budget. Three lecture hours per week. Scheduled field trips are required.
BIOL 450.subject: BIOL
BIOL 450.title: Principles of Biological Oceanography

BIOL 460.description: Functional physiology of human organ systems.
BIOL 460.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302 or MSCI 311.
BIOL 460.subject: BIOL
BIOL 460.title: Advanced Human Physiology

BIOL 460L.description: Experiments on organ system functions using different animal models.
BIOL 460L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 460L.title: Advanced Human Physiology Laboratory

BIOL 461.description: Structure, function, and development of human anatomy.
BIOL 461.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in any two of the following: BIOL 301, BIOL 302, or BIOL 303.
BIOL 461.subject: BIOL
BIOL 461.title: Advanced Human Anatomy

BIOL 461L.description: Practical exercises in structure, function, and development of anatomy using digital and animal models.
BIOL 461L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 461L.title: Advanced Human Anatomy Laboratory

BIOL 462.description: The taxonomy, morphology, metabolism, genetics, and ecology of microorganisms.
BIOL 462.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302.
BIOL 462.subject: BIOL
BIOL 462.title: Advanced Microbiology

BIOL 462L.description: Practical exercises with the taxonomy, morphology, metabolism, genetics, and ecology of microorganisms.
BIOL 462L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 462L.title: Advanced Microbiology Laboratory

BIOL 465.description: Elements of nutrition and animal feeding in veterinary practice. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 465.subject: BIOL
BIOL 465.title: Domestic Animal Nutrition

BIOL 497.description: Student seminars and a survey of research in the fields of Biological Sciences.
BIOL 497.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 301, BIOL 302, and BIOL 303, or Instructor's Permission
BIOL 497.subject: BIOL
BIOL 497.title: Undergraduate Seminar in Biological Sciences

BIOL 498.description: Methodologies of biological research with emphasis on hypothesis formation, research design, and data collection, and current issues in biology.
BIOL 498.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in any BIOL 300-level or higher laboratory course; C or higher in any two of BIOL 301, BIOL 302, and BIOL 303.
BIOL 498.subject: BIOL
BIOL 498.title: Introduction to Biological Research

BIOL 499.description: Supervised training in Biological Sciences conducting experiments, analyzing data, and solving scientific problems. Contract required.
BIOL 499.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 399.
BIOL 499.subject: BIOL
BIOL 499.title: Practicum in Biological Sciences

BIOL 502.description: An overview of the microbial world including a survey of the distribution, functioning, and diversity of microorganisms in natural systems. Discusses the crucial roles that microorganisms play in ecosystem function, biogeochemical cycles, and environmental quality.
BIOL 502.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 102 or BIOL 102; C or better in CHEM 112.
BIOL 502.subject: BIOL
BIOL 502.title: Environmental Microbiology

BIOL 505.description: An introduction to how cell-cell communication, gene expression, cell division, cytoskeletal dynamics, and interactions with the extracellular matrix result in the differentiation, pattern formation, morphogenesis, and growth necessary to generate a new individual.
BIOL 505.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302.
BIOL 505.subject: BIOL
BIOL 505.title: Developmental Biology

BIOL 505L.description: Descriptive and experimental exercises related to embryology. One three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 505L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 505L.title: Developmental Biology Laboratory I

BIOL 506.description: Molecular aspects of development from gamete formation through tissue and organ differentiation in plants and animals. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 506.subject: BIOL
BIOL 506.title: Developmental Biology II

BIOL 506L.description: A series of experimentally oriented laboratory exercises will be performed. One three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 506L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 506L.title: Developmental Biology Laboratory II

BIOL 508.description: An introduction to the processes involved in normal human embryology and how genetic and environmental disruptions result in congenital disorders.
BIOL 508.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 302 and BIOL 303.
BIOL 508.subject: BIOL
BIOL 508.title: Human Embryology

BIOL 510.description: Phylogenetic and comparative aspects of anatomy, physiology, reproduction, and embryology of the invertebrates. Three lecture and one three-hour laboratory period per week.
BIOL 510.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
BIOL 510.subject: BIOL
BIOL 510.title: Invertebrate Zoology

BIOL 523.description: Descriptive and molecular examination of the processes and mechanisms used by plants in organogenesis, differentiation, and morphogenesis. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 523.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302 and BIOL 303.
BIOL 523.subject: BIOL
BIOL 523.title: Plant Development

BIOL 523L.description: Experiments utilizing a genetic approach to the study of plant development. Three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 523L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 523L.title: Plant Developmental Laboratory

BIOL 524.description: Taxonomy and morphology of fungi; cultivation, life histories, and economic importance; all classes and major orders considered. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 524.subject: BIOL
BIOL 524.title: Mycology

BIOL 525.description: Diversity, distribution, physiology, ecology, evolution, and economic importance of marine algal, seagrass, and mangrove communities. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips are required.
BIOL 525.subject: BIOL
BIOL 525.title: Marine Plants

BIOL 526.description: Two lecture and four laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 526.subject: BIOL
BIOL 526.title: The Fall Flora

BIOL 527.description: Two lecture and four laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 527.subject: BIOL
BIOL 527.title: The Spring Flora

BIOL 528.description: Two lecture and four laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 528.subject: BIOL
BIOL 528.title: The Summer Flora

BIOL 530.description: An introduction to the tissues that make up the human body. The microscopic anatomy of tissues is examined and discussed in terms of function and physiology. Three lecture hours and four laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 530.subject: BIOL
BIOL 530.title: Histology

BIOL 531.description: Parasites of biological, economic, and public health importance. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 531.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: 300 level Biology course or equivalent.
BIOL 531.subject: BIOL
BIOL 531.title: Parasitology

BIOL 532.description: The evolutionary ecology of reptiles and amphibians, as well as conservation biology of the major groups, global diversity of herpetofauna, with emphasis on reptiles and amphibians of the southeastern US.
BIOL 532.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301.
BIOL 532.subject: BIOL
BIOL 532.title: Herpetology

BIOL 534.description: A comparative survey of behavior patterns of animals from protists to humans and the physiological mechanisms underlying behavior.
BIOL 534.subject: BIOL
BIOL 534.title: Animal Behavior

BIOL 534L.description: Observational and experimental methods used in classifying animal behavior patterns and in determining underlying control mechanisms. One three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 534L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 534L.title: Animal Behavior Laboratory

BIOL 535.description: Management and conservation of aquatic and marine resources, with emphasis on fisheries. Data procurement and analysis; commercial and recreational fisheries; sociological, political, legal, and environmental factors that affect fishery management; and fish biodiversity.
BIOL 535.subject: BIOL
BIOL 535.title: Fishery Management

BIOL 536.description: Phylogeny, morphology, behavior, and ecology of fishes. Three lecture and 3 laboratory hours plus three field trips to be arranged.
BIOL 536.subject: BIOL
BIOL 536.title: Ichthyology

BIOL 537.description: Introduction to the practical and scientific aspects of the commercial culture of freshwater and marine organisms. Three lecture hours per week. One all-day field trip required.
BIOL 537.subject: BIOL
BIOL 537.title: Aquaculture

BIOL 538.description: The identification of behavioral adaptations of estuarine and marine organisms: their ecology, physiology, development, and evolutionary history; field observations.
BIOL 538.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 101 and BIOL 102 or MSCI 311.
BIOL 538.subject: BIOL
BIOL 538.title: Behavior of Marine Organisms

BIOL 541.description: Description of biological macromolecules and major metabolic pathways.
BIOL 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334.
BIOL 541.subject: BIOL
BIOL 541.title: Biochemistry

BIOL 541L.description: Experiments and demonstrations illustrating the principles of biochemistry. Three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 541L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 541L.title: Biochemistry Laboratory

BIOL 543.description: An integrative and comparative study of the structure, function, and evolution of the physiological systems of animals. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 543.subject: BIOL
BIOL 543.title: Comparative Physiology

BIOL 543L.description: Laboratory exercises to illustrate principles from BIOL 543 . Three hours per week.
BIOL 543L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 543L.title: Comparative Physiology Laboratory

BIOL 545.description: Comprehensive introduction to the structure and function of major biological macromolecules—amino acids, proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids. Topics include enzyme catalysis, kinetics, inhibition, and core metabolic pathways such as glycolysis, gluconeogenesis, the citric acid cycle, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid metabolism, and amino acid metabolism. Concludes with an integrated study of mammalian fuel metabolism and the regulation and coordination of metabolic pathways.
BIOL 545.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 334, or departmental permission.
BIOL 545.subject: BIOL
BIOL 545.title: Protein Biochemistry and Metabolism

BIOL 546.description: Examination of key topics in molecular biology, including DNA and RNA metabolism, regulation of gene expression at transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels, protein synthesis, and mechanisms of cell cycle control and cancer development. Includes principles and applications of recombinant DNA technology.
BIOL 546.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 302, or departmental approval.
BIOL 546.subject: BIOL
BIOL 546.title: Molecular Biochemistry of the Cell

BIOL 549.description: A general survey of the major physiological processes in plants. Two lecture and four laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 549.subject: BIOL
BIOL 549.title: Plant Physiology

BIOL 550.description: Introduction to bacteria and viruses emphasizing ultrastructure, physiology, genetics, and growth. Discussion of public health, industrial, and environmental microbiology. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 550.subject: BIOL
BIOL 550.title: Bacteriology

BIOL 552.description: An introduction to the principles of population genetics, with emphasis on the origin, maintenance, and significance of genetic variation in natural populations.
BIOL 552.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
BIOL 552.subject: BIOL
BIOL 552.title: Population Genetics

BIOL 553.description: Current concepts and applications of genomics, addressing questions from throughout biological inquiry.
BIOL 553.subject: BIOL
BIOL 553.title: Genomics

BIOL 555.description: An examination of the differences between genetic and epigenetic influences on gene expression, epigenetic mechanisms that regulate gene expression, how epigenetic modifications are propagated, and the phenotypic consequences of abnormal epigenetic regulation in disease, development, and evolution.
BIOL 555.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302 and BIOL 303 or permission of the department.
BIOL 555.subject: BIOL
BIOL 555.title: Epigenetics

BIOL 558.description: Discussion of how physiological factors, like nutritional status, influence systemic signals to alter stem cell activity, and the physiological stimuli that impact stem cell activity in a variety of organisms (from worms to humans).
BIOL 558.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C of higher in BIOL 302.
BIOL 558.subject: BIOL
BIOL 558.title: Stem Cells and The Physiological Environment

BIOL 570.description: Interactions of organisms and the environment; ecosystem structure and functions. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 570.subject: BIOL
BIOL 570.title: Principles of Ecology

BIOL 571.description: Principles of conservation biology. Importance of biodiversity, causes of decline and extinction, and restoration and conversation policy in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
BIOL 571.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301.
BIOL 571.subject: BIOL
BIOL 571.title: Conservation Biology

BIOL 572.description: Quantitative study of the population, community and evolutionary ecology of freshwater habitats (lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, wetlands). Includes mandatory fieldtrips.
BIOL 572.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301.
BIOL 572.subject: BIOL
BIOL 572.title: Freshwater Ecology

BIOL 573.description: Processes governing insect ecology (distribution, abundance, population regulation, community assembly, and diversity patterns across the globe), and investigations of the life-history, behavior, and development of South Carolina insects.
BIOL 573.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 301 or MSCI 311, or permission of the instructor.
BIOL 573.subject: BIOL
BIOL 573.title: Insect Ecology

BIOL 574.description: Exploration of how human activities affect marine natural populations, species, communities and ecosystems, including threats to biodiversity; approaches to marine conservation; and ecological and evolutionary responses to anthropogenic disturbance.
BIOL 574.subject: BIOL
BIOL 574.title: Marine Conservation Biology

BIOL 575.description: Structure, dynamics, and interactions between populations and communities in marine ecosystems. Attendance at designated departmental seminars is required. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 575.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: CHEM 111 and BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
BIOL 575.subject: BIOL
BIOL 575.title: Marine Ecology

BIOL 575L.description: Laboratory and field exercises in coastal environments. Three hours per week plus field trips.
BIOL 575L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 575L.title: Marine Ecology Laboratory

BIOL 576.description: Interdisciplinary examination of the distribution, reproduction, survival, and historical variation of the principal commercial marine fisheries.
BIOL 576.subject: BIOL
BIOL 576.title: Marine Fisheries Ecology

BIOL 577.description: Structure, productivity, and biodiversity of coral reefs, emphasizing their sensitivity, stability, and sustainability. Taught as an extended field experience with daily lectures and guided research activities.
BIOL 577.subject: BIOL
BIOL 577.title: Ecology of Coral Reefs

BIOL 588.description: This course focuses on quantitative knowledge for interdisciplinary applications in genetics as well as hands-on experience in analyzing genetic data. In this course, students will have programming exercises in using analysis tools to conduct genome-wide analysis, annotation, and interpretation of genetic data using R/Bioconductor packages.
BIOL 588.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in STAT 201 or higher.
BIOL 588.subject: BIOL
BIOL 588.title: Genomic Data Science

BIOL 599.description: Current developments in biological sciences. Readings and research on selected topics. Course content varies and will be announced in the schedule of classes by title.
BIOL 599.subject: BIOL
BIOL 599.title: Topics in Biology

BIOL 610.description: Survey of current concepts regarding the molecular and genetic factors that regulate the origin and progression of cancer. Readings based on current primary literature.
BIOL 610.subject: BIOL
BIOL 610.title: Hallmarks of Cancer

BIOL 612.description: Advanced study of viruses with regard to biochemical, molecular, pathological, epidemiological, and biotechnological aspects. Focus on animal viruses with particular emphasis on human pathogens.
BIOL 612.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302.
BIOL 612.subject: BIOL
BIOL 612.title: Virology - Classical and Emerging Concepts

BIOL 614.description: Focuses on the understanding of how stem cells can be used to make fundamental biological discoveries with a special focus in neuroscience.
BIOL 614.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302.
BIOL 614.subject: BIOL
BIOL 614.title: Stem Cell Biology

BIOL 620.description: Basic immunological concepts including antibody structure, function, and genetics; cellular immunology; transplantation; hypersensitivity; autoimmunity; and immunity to infectious diseases.
BIOL 620.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 302.
BIOL 620.subject: BIOL
BIOL 620.title: Immunobiology

BIOL 625.description: Advanced study of infectious diseases caused by fungi. Etiology, symptoms, and treatment of fungi related illnesses.
BIOL 625.subject: BIOL
BIOL 625.title: Medical Mycology

BIOL 627.description: Examines the physiology and ecology of phytoplankton, including environmental controls on community composition, primary productivity, and detection and characterization of water quality (eutrophication) and harmful algal blooms.
BIOL 627.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MSCI 102 or MSCI 450 or BIOL 450.
BIOL 627.subject: BIOL
BIOL 627.title: Marine Phytoplankton

BIOL 630.description: Biology of birds at molecular, organismal, and population levels, emphasizing unique adaptations of the class of Aves.
BIOL 630.subject: BIOL
BIOL 630.title: Biology of Birds

BIOL 633.description: An overview of neurodevelopmental disorders, focusing on the known genetic and environmental mechanisms leading to altered nervous system function. Discussion for each disorder will include how the nervous system is altered, the underlying biological mechanisms, and current/future treatments. Includes discussion of scientific journal articles.
BIOL 633.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 302.
BIOL 633.subject: BIOL
BIOL 633.title: Biology of Human Neurodevelopmental Disorders

BIOL 634.description: Advances in molecular and cellular neurobiology that bring new understanding for human neurological disease.
BIOL 634.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 302 and SCHC 330 or BIOL 405.
BIOL 634.subject: BIOL
BIOL 634.title: Biology of Neurological Diseases

BIOL 635.description: Descriptive and computational exploration of the molecules, cells, and circuits in the nervous systems of animals that make observable behaviors possible.
BIOL 635.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 302.
BIOL 635.subject: BIOL
BIOL 635.title: Neurophysiology

BIOL 635L.description: Experimental investigation of the neurons and neural circuits that underlie observable behaviors in animals.
BIOL 635L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 635L.title: Neurophysiology Laboratory

BIOL 636.description: An introduction to the integrative and comparative study of animal sensory systems.
BIOL 636.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in BIOL 301 and BIOL 302.
BIOL 636.subject: BIOL
BIOL 636.title: Sensory Biology

BIOL 640.description: Interactions of microorganisms with each other, with more complex organisms, and with their environments. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 640.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 550 and either BIOL 301 or MSCI 311.
BIOL 640.subject: BIOL
BIOL 640.title: Microbial Ecology

BIOL 641.description: This course examines how the mechanisms by which animals and plants interact with their physical environments influence organismal physiology.
BIOL 641.subject: BIOL
BIOL 641.title: Biophysical Ecology

BIOL 650.description: Advanced study of related aspects of biological evolution. Rose of life from physical and chemical precursors, biochemical basis of adaptation to ecological pressures, and biochemical aspects of the origins and maintenance of biodiversity.
BIOL 650.subject: BIOL
BIOL 650.title: Biochemical Evolution

BIOL 651.description: A study of the aquatic environment and its biota. Three lecture and four laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 651.subject: BIOL
BIOL 651.title: Limnology

BIOL 652.description: An advanced course in evolutionary biology, including natural selection, neutral evolution, molecular evolution population genetics, quantitative genetics, sexual selection, speciation, human evolution, and the evolution of disease.
BIOL 652.subject: BIOL
BIOL 652.title: Evolutionary Biology

BIOL 653.description: Studies of the principles of genetics and molecular biology as applied to adaptive evolution of genes and genomes.
BIOL 653.subject: BIOL
BIOL 653.title: Bioinformatics

BIOL 654.description: Speciation as the source of biological diversity. Analysis of genetic and ecological models of speciation using primary literature.
BIOL 654.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOL 301 and BIOL 303.
BIOL 654.subject: BIOL
BIOL 654.title: Speciation and the Origin of Biodiversity

BIOL 655.description: Studies in molecular biology and genetics with emphasis on the use of newly developed techniques in biotechnology. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 655.subject: BIOL
BIOL 655.title: Biotechnology

BIOL 656.description: Techniques used in biotechnology will be employed in the context of an experimental project. Twelve laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 656.subject: BIOL
BIOL 656.title: Experimental Biotechnology

BIOL 660.description: Evolution, systematics, genetics, ecology, and adaptation of mammals. Emphasis on native South Carolina species. Two lectures and one two-hour laboratory per week, plus five field trips to be arranged.
BIOL 660.subject: BIOL
BIOL 660.title: Biology of Mammals

BIOL 662.description: Signaling pathways involved in human diseases, such as cancer, AIDS, autoimmune diseases and diabetes, and cellular processes involving apoptosis, cell cycle, cell-cell adhesion, growth factors, hormones, G protein-couples receptors, cytokines and immune response.
BIOL 662.subject: BIOL
BIOL 662.title: Signal Transduction and Pathogenesis

BIOL 665.description: Molecular mechanisms underlying gene action and differentiation in man; the genetic bases for human variability and inborn metabolic errors leading to inherited diseases.
BIOL 665.subject: BIOL
BIOL 665.title: Human Molecular Genetics

BIOL 667.description: An advanced examination of the molecular mechanisms underlying gene action in humans. Current literature illustrating the genotype-phenotype relationship in human disease pathogenesis will be discussed.
BIOL 667.subject: BIOL
BIOL 667.title: Molecular and Genetic Mechanisms of Disease Pathogenesis

BIOL 668.description: Core concepts of biochemistry as applied to human health and disease.
BIOL 668.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in CHEM 555/BIOL 545 or CHEM 550/BIOL 541.
BIOL 668.subject: BIOL
BIOL 668.title: Metabolic Biochemistry of Human Disease

BIOL 671.description: Physiological, molecular, and genetic examination of induced plant responses to various biotic and abiotic environmental stresses.
BIOL 671.subject: BIOL
BIOL 671.title: Plant Responses to the Environment

BIOL 690.description: Theoretical and practical aspects of scanning and transmission electron microscopy, digital image acquisition and energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Two lecture and one laboratory hour per week, plus a research project to be arranged.
BIOL 690.subject: BIOL
BIOL 690.title: Ultramicroscopy

BIOL 701.description: Selected biochemical topics emphasizing research literature. One lecture hour per credit per week.
BIOL 701.subject: BIOL
BIOL 701.title: Selected Topics in Biochemistr

BIOL 702.description: Selected botanical topics emphasizing research literature. One lecture hour per credit per week.
BIOL 702.subject: BIOL
BIOL 702.title: Selected Topics in Plant Biology

BIOL 703.description: Selected ecology topics emphasizing research literature. One lecture hour per credit per week.
BIOL 703.subject: BIOL
BIOL 703.title: Selected Topics in Ecology

BIOL 704.description: Selected genetic and developmental biology topics emphasizing research literature. One lecture hour per credit per week.
BIOL 704.subject: BIOL
BIOL 704.title: Selected Topics in Genetics and Developmental Biology

BIOL 705.description: Selected zoological topics emphasizing research literature. One lecture hour per credit per week.
BIOL 705.subject: BIOL
BIOL 705.title: Selected Topics in Zoology

BIOL 710.description: This course is designed to increase teaching proficiency on the science behind student learning, scientific teaching, assessments and rubrics, active learning, project-based learning, teaching technology, inclusive teaching and universal design, classroom and course management, and course design. Participants will begin to develop their own set of course content (specific to their area of expertise) and will deliver that course content as the designated instructor of record after completion of this course. Students will also develop a proper syllabus for their designated course and prepare their own teaching philosophy at the end of this course.
BIOL 710.subject: BIOL
BIOL 710.title: Scientific Teaching and Pedagogy

BIOL 711.description: A detailed study of nucleic acids including their structure/chemistry, biosynthesis, processing, and biological functions.
BIOL 711.subject: BIOL
BIOL 711.title: Structure and Function of Nucleic Acids

BIOL 712.description: Advanced topics in Mendelian genetics, DNA repair/recombination, and mechanisms of gene expression. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 712.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 303 or equivalent and BIOL 711.
BIOL 712.subject: BIOL
BIOL 712.title: DNA Transactions and Gene Expression

BIOL 714.description: Problems of cellular organization, interactions, and control. Cell growth and death, cell-cell recognition and communication, intracellular transport, the structure and assembly of cellular organelles, somatic cell genetics, and evolution of cells. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 714.subject: BIOL
BIOL 714.title: Advanced Cell Biology

BIOL 717.description: A comprehensive treatment of the chemistry, metabolism, regulation, and function of biological systems.
BIOL 717.subject: BIOL
BIOL 717.title: Biological Chemistry

BIOL 718.description: A continuation of BIOL 717 . Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 718.subject: BIOL
BIOL 718.title: Biological Chemistry II

BIOL 722.description: The ecology and physiology of freshwater and marine bacteria. The functions of bacteria in aquatic habitats and the public health aspects of pollution as they relate to microbiology. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 722.subject: BIOL
BIOL 722.title: Aquatic Bacteriology

BIOL 725.description: Two lectures and two laboratory periods per week.
BIOL 725.subject: BIOL
BIOL 725.title: Embryology of Angiosperms

BIOL 726.description: Two lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 726.subject: BIOL
BIOL 726.title: Soil-Plant Relationships

BIOL 727.description: Three lecture hours and one three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 727.subject: BIOL
BIOL 727.title: Marine Phytoplankton

BIOL 728.description: Three lecture hours and one three-hour laboratory per week.
BIOL 728.subject: BIOL
BIOL 728.title: Advanced Phycology

BIOL 730.description: One seminar and six laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 730.subject: BIOL
BIOL 730.title: The Biology of Fish

BIOL 731.description: Principles of systematics and an in-depth study of invertebrate phylogeny and ecology. Two lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 731.subject: BIOL
BIOL 731.title: Advanced Invertebrate Zoology I

BIOL 734.description: Three lectures or conferences per week.
BIOL 734.subject: BIOL
BIOL 734.title: The Vertebrates

BIOL 736.description: The biochemical and molecular mechanisms by which a variety of organisms develop. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 736.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 340 or BIOL 505, or equivalent.
BIOL 736.subject: BIOL
BIOL 736.title: Advanced Developmental Biology

BIOL 741.description: Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 741.subject: BIOL
BIOL 741.title: Fungal Physiology

BIOL 748.description: A brief introduction to general endocrinology followed by an in-depth examination of the molecular mechanisms of hormone action, including receptors, second messengers, and hormonal control of transcription/translation. The evolution of hormone-receptor systems will also be examined.
BIOL 748.subject: BIOL
BIOL 748.title: Molecular Endocrinology

BIOL 749.description: Team-taught course on the theory and practice of laboratory techniques for investigating the structure and function of cellular components, especially organelles, proteins, and nucleic acids. Three lecture hours per week. Lectures will be supplemented with laboratory demonstrations.
BIOL 749.subject: BIOL
BIOL 749.title: Methods in Molecular and Cell Biology

BIOL 752.description: Biological, geological, and physical processes that influence the cyling of major bioactive elements (C, O, N, P, S) in marine waters and sediments.
BIOL 752.subject: BIOL
BIOL 752.title: Marine Biogeochemistry

BIOL 753.description: The action of genes in development and differentiation at the molecular, cellular, and organ (tissue) levels, with examples taken from microorganisms, plants, animals, and man. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 753.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOL 350 and two semesters of biochemistry or equivalents.
BIOL 753.subject: BIOL
BIOL 753.title: Developmental Genetics

BIOL 754.description: Shipboard experience with basic techniques used by geological, physical, chemical, and biological oceanographers.
BIOL 754.subject: BIOL
BIOL 754.title: Oceanographic Techniques

BIOL 755.description: An intensive field course centered around field problems in a variety of habitats (freshwater, terrestrial, estuarine). Students will use a variety of quantitative sampling methods to test ecological hypotheses on several two-day field trips.
BIOL 755.subject: BIOL
BIOL 755.title: Quantitative Ecology

BIOL 757.description: An intensive consideration of topics of current interest in biology. One lecture hour per credit per week.
BIOL 757.subject: BIOL
BIOL 757.title: Special Topics in Biology

BIOL 758.description: Appropriate designation will be made for the particular program in any given semester.
BIOL 758.subject: BIOL
BIOL 758.title: Research

BIOL 759.description: Two lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 759.subject: BIOL
BIOL 759.title: Physiological Ecology

BIOL 760.description: Theory and design of modern electron microscopes; advancement in the theory and practice of specimen preparation of biological materials; interpretation of ultrastructure of cells and tissues. Three lecture hours a week.
BIOL 760.subject: BIOL
BIOL 760.title: Electron Microscopy

BIOL 762.description: A survey of the structure and function of wetland ecosystems emphasizing the current literature.
BIOL 762.subject: BIOL
BIOL 762.title: Wetlands Ecology

BIOL 763.description: Three lecture and two laboratory hours per week.
BIOL 763.subject: BIOL
BIOL 763.title: Biology of Populations

BIOL 764.description: Study of modern advances in plant physiology. Plant biotechnology topics, such as tissue culture, nitrogen fixation, photosynthesis, weed and pest control, molecular cloning, and genetic manipulation. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 764.subject: BIOL
BIOL 764.title: Advanced Plant Physiology

BIOL 765.description: Theoretical bases of ecology are explored from current literature with topics from organismal, populational, community, and ecosystem approaches. Principles for the construction and testing of hypotheses and models.
BIOL 765.subject: BIOL
BIOL 765.title: Theoretical Ecology

BIOL 766.description: Theoretical and empirical studies of the evolutionary process. Historical perspective of major developments in evolution as well as modern quantitative and ecological genetic studies.
BIOL 766.subject: BIOL
BIOL 766.title: Evolutionary Biology

BIOL 768.description: Concepts in systems ecology and ecological modeling. Emphasis on the use of models and computer simulations in examining environmental interactions, predicting environmental impact, and facilitating the process of environmental planning. Lab practice in model development and computer simulation analysis.
BIOL 768.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 111 or equivalent, ecology, ENHS 660.
BIOL 768.subject: BIOL
BIOL 768.title: Ecological Modeling and Environmental Planning

BIOL 769.description: Theoretical aspects and examples of the variety of reproductive and life history patterns found in animals and plants as adaptations to various environmental constraints. Three lecture hours per week.
BIOL 769.subject: BIOL
BIOL 769.title: Reproductive Ecology

BIOL 770.description: Recent developments in cellular and molecular biology including genetic mechanisms, ultrastructure, and function of organelles and membranes. Lectures supplemented with readings from current literature. Primarily for the MAT program. Not available for MS or PhD credit in biology.
BIOL 770.subject: BIOL
BIOL 770.title: Current Topics in Molecular Biology

BIOL 771.description: Concepts of growth, differentiation, and morphogenesis of organisms in light of recent advances in biological knowledge. Lectures supplemented with readings from current literature. Primarily for the M.A.T. program. Not available for M.S. or Ph.D. credit in biology.
BIOL 771.subject: BIOL
BIOL 771.title: Current Topics in Developmental Biology

BIOL 772.description: Ecological concepts with reference to recent advances in environmental sciences. Special attention to the ecology of the coast, swamps, and other habitats of importance in the Southeast. Primarily for the M.A.T. program. Not available for M.S. or Ph.D. credit in biology.
BIOL 772.subject: BIOL
BIOL 772.title: Current Topics in Ecology

BIOL 775.description: Introduction to the major forms of plant life in the state. Includes fungi, algae, bryophytes, and vascular plants. Lecture-laboratory-field course primarily for the M.A.T. program. Not available for M.S. or Ph.D. credit in biology.
BIOL 775.subject: BIOL
BIOL 775.title: Plants of South Carolina

BIOL 776.description: Introduction to the major forms of animal life in the state. Animals will be studied and/or collected in their native habitat. Includes identification, behavior, and ecology of animals with emphasis on vertebrates. Lecture-laboratory-field course primarily for the M.A.T. program. Not available for M.S. or Ph.D. credit in biology.
BIOL 776.subject: BIOL
BIOL 776.title: Animals of South Carolina

BIOL 798.description: Directed laboratory research and readings in the biological sciences for M.S. and Ph.D. students prior to preparation of theses and dissertations.
BIOL 798.subject: BIOL
BIOL 798.title: Research in Biology

BIOL 801.description: Assigned readings in special topics in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology followed by classroom discussions. Designed to teach critical analysis of the scientific literature.
BIOL 801.subject: BIOL
BIOL 801.title: Directed Readings in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology

BIOL 802.description: A review of current literature in plant biology involving student presentations of seminars. One discussion hour per credit per week. The course may be repeated for credit.
BIOL 802.subject: BIOL
BIOL 802.title: Seminar in Plant Biology

BIOL 803.description: A review of current literature in ecology involving student presentations of seminars. One discussion hour per credit per week.
BIOL 803.subject: BIOL
BIOL 803.title: Seminar in Ecology

BIOL 804.description: Student presentations of papers from the current literature in molecular, cellular, and developmental biology. Designed to give experience in oral presentations. May be repeated.
BIOL 804.subject: BIOL
BIOL 804.title: Seminar in Molecular, Cellular, and Developmental Biology

BIOL 805.description: A review of current literature in zoology involving student presentations of seminars. One discussion hour per credit per week.
BIOL 805.subject: BIOL
BIOL 805.title: Seminar in Zoology

BIOL 806.description: Recent trends in biological research from the perspective of individual faculty members in the department. May be repeated.
BIOL 806.subject: BIOL
BIOL 806.title: Perspectives in Biological Research

BIOL 809.description: Research in biology requires diverse skills, many of which are not formally taught. Students will develop essential skills in science communication, presentation, writing and peer review. This course is designed for Masters and PhD students.
BIOL 809.subject: BIOL
BIOL 809.title: Communication in Biological Research
